extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, EPA reviewers, and owners/operators of affected electric generating units (EGUs)
extracted.subtask_short: EPA emission guidelines compliance for EGUs
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluative criteria that states and affected EGUs must meet to implement and demonstrate compliance with the EPA's emission guidelines for steam-generating EGUs, including increments of progress, reporting milestones, monitoring/QA, CCS-specific reporting, and permitted compliance flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF extension documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a state seeks to apply a longer compliance schedule based on Remaining Useful Life Of Facility (RULOF), the state should provide documentation to justify why it is unreasonable for the affected EGU to meet the emission guideline compliance schedule even with an additional 1-year extension, demonstrating the need for the longer schedule was due to circumstances outside the affected EGU's control and that the affected EGU met all relevant increments of progress and other obligations in a timely manner up to the point of delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should demonstrate circumstances are not self-created. Helpful evidence includes permits obtained and/or contracts entered into for installation of control technology, receipts, invoices, and correspondence with vendors and regulators. See 40 CFR 60.24a(e)(1) considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised schedule must be no longer than necessary (40 CFR 60.24a(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: In establishing a longer compliance schedule pursuant to 40 CFR 60.24a(f)(1), a state must demonstrate that the revised schedule is no longer than necessary to accommodate the circumstances that resulted in the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must justify the duration of any extension with supporting evidence tied to the actual delay-causing circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: IoP threshold (when Increments of Progress required)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include legally enforceable Increments of Progress (IoPs) when the final compliance deadline is more than the regulatory threshold after plan submission (subpart Ba requires IoPs when final compliance is more than 20 months after plan submittal). These emission guidelines set a 24-month plan submission deadline, triggering IoP requirements for relevant subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IoPs appropriate for BSERs involving substantial planning/construction (e.g., CCS, natural gas co-firing) to assure steady progress and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion and constraints for assigning IoP dates
rubrics_metrics.description: States may choose calendar dates for all IoPs for long- and medium-term coal-fired EGUs, subject to two constraints: (1) the IoP for 40 CFR 60.21a(h)(1) (submission of final control plan) must be the earliest calendar date among increments, and (2) the IoP for 40 CFR 60.21a(h)(5) (final compliance) must be aligned with the compliance date for the subcategory (Jan 1, 2032 for long-term; Jan 1, 2030 for medium-term).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides flexibility to tailor timelines to individual facilities while ensuring key milestones precede final compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption of natural gas- and oil-fired subcategories from IoPs
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural gas- and oil-fired EGU subcategories are exempted from IoP requirements because their BSERs are routine operation and maintenance, not requiring installation of significant new emission controls or operational changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States need not adopt IoPs for units whose compliance does not involve significant new construction or complex implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to particularize IoPs to chosen compliance approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Units adopting the BSER specified for their subcategory (CCS for long-term, natural gas co-firing for medium-term) must use BSER-specific IoPs tailored to those BSERs; units using other control technologies must adopt increments corresponding to the steps in 40 CFR 60.21a(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States will particularize generic subpart Ba IoPs as appropriate for units that comply with technologies other than the BSER associated with the subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipeline-specific IoPs and sequestration-site IoP
rubrics_metrics.description: States must include additional IoPs specific to pipeline construction for both long- and medium-term coal-fired subcategories, and an additional IoP related to identification of an appropriate sequestration site for the long-term subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These increments ensure timely progress on planning, permitting, and construction activities related to pipelines and sequestration that may be required for full compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of IoP activities and documentation to public website
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must require affected EGUs with IoPs to post the activities or actions that constitute the increments, the schedule required in the state plan for achieving them, and, within 30 business days, any documentation necessary to demonstrate that they have been achieved to the Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This posting requirement promotes transparency. See section X.E.1.b.ii of the preamble for additional discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term (CCS) subcategory: seven enforceable IoPs
rubrics_metrics.description: For coal-fired steam generating units in the long-term subcategory adopting CCS, the seven IoPs are: (1) submission of a final control plan (must include feasibility/FEED study, anticipated timeline, benchmarks); (2) awarding of contracts or issuance of orders for emission control systems or component parts; (3) initiation of onsite construction/installation required to achieve 90% CO2 capture on an annual basis; (4) completion of onsite construction/installation required to achieve 90% CO2 capture on an annual basis; (5) demonstration that all permitting actions related to pipeline construction have commenced (with planning/design documentation, complete list of pipeline-related permit applications, attestation of completeness, and timeline); (6) submittal of report identifying geographic sequestration location, transport method, regulatory requirements, and permitting timeline; (7) final compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must assign calendar deadlines so that the first increment (submission of final control plan) is the earliest and final compliance (seventh increment) is set for January 1, 2032.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term units adopting other compliance approaches: adopt subpart Ba IoPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal-fired long-term units that adopt a compliance approach different from CCS must adopt IoPs consistent with the generic increments at 40 CFR 60.21a(h), with the first increment being the earliest and final compliance set for January 1, 2032.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States particularize the generic IoPs to reflect the alternative control strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term (natural gas co-firing) subcategory: six enforceable IoPs
rubrics_metrics.description: For coal-fired steam generating units in the medium-term subcategory adopting natural gas co-firing, the six IoPs are: (1) submission of a final control plan (must include design basis for modifications, anticipated timeline, benchmarks); (2) awarding of contracts for boiler modifications or issuance of purchase orders; (3) initiation of onsite construction/installation necessary to enable natural gas co-firing at 40% annual average; (4) completion of onsite construction for co-firing capability; (5) demonstration that all permitting actions related to pipeline construction have commenced (with planning/design documentation, complete list of pipeline-related permit applications, attestation of completeness, and timeline); (6) final compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must assign calendar deadlines so the first increment is earliest and final compliance (sixth increment) is set for January 1, 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term units adopting other compliance approaches: adopt subpart Ba IoPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal-fired medium-term units that adopt compliance approaches different from natural gas co-firing must adopt IoPs consistent with 40 CFR 60.21a(h), with the first increment being the earliest and final compliance set for January 1, 2030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States particularize the IoPs for alternative strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: IoP date adjustments when compliance date extension approved
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected EGU receives approval for a compliance date extension, the date for one or more IoPs must be adjusted to align with the revised compliance date; the new dates for relevant IoPs must be specified in the extension application. The last increment—final compliance—should be no later than 1 year after the original compliance date, per section X.C.1.d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions require updating IoP calendar deadlines in the extension application and still respect the one-year post-original-date ceiling for final compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of state plan revisions to accommodate changes (40 CFR 60.28a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan revisions (including to subcategory assignments and corresponding IoPs) may be used, at a state's discretion, to account for changes in planned compliance approaches, RULOF-based adjustments, and timeline modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subpart Ba optional state plan revision process provides planning flexibility to respond to changed circumstances or switches in control strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and milestones for EGUs planning to permanently cease operations (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs assigned to the medium-term subcategory and those invoking RULOF based on remaining useful life that plan to permanently cease operations must submit milestone reports: an Initial Milestone Report five years before the planned cessation date (or 60 days after state plan submission, whichever is later), annual Milestone Status Reports for each intervening year, and a Final Milestone Status Report no later than six months after the committed cessation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reporting obligations provide transparency and assurance that voluntary commitments to cease operations (which affect applicable standards) are being carried out and can signal when plan revisions may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Milestone Report required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Initial Milestone Report must include: (1) a summary of process steps required to permanently cease operation by the state-plan date, including approximate timing/duration and notification requirements; (2) a list of key milestones and calendar deadlines (must include initial notice to relevant reliability authority and official retirement filing with reliability authority); (3) an analysis comparing these timelines to similar EGUs in the state that permanently ceased operations within the prior 10 years; (4) supporting regulatory documents and filings (correspondence/filings with RTO/ISO/balancing authority/PUC, deactivation-related reliability assessments, SEC filings, integrated resource plans, PUC orders, reliability analyses, notifications altering timing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States will select certain process steps to serve as milestones; the report must demonstrate the plan and provide documentary support for planned retirement steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Milestone Status Report required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each intervening year prior to cessation, the owner/operator must submit an annual Milestone Status Report addressing: (1) progress toward meeting all milestones identified in the Initial Milestone Report; and (2) supporting regulatory documents and relevant SEC filings, including correspondence and official filings with applicable authorities to demonstrate compliance or progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reports track timely progress and provide supporting documentation for transparency and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Milestone Status Report required contents and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within six months following the committed closure date, the affected EGU must submit a Final Milestone Status Report documenting any actions taken subsequent to ceasing operation to ensure cessation is permanent, including any regulatory filings with applicable authorities or decommissioning plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This report confirms permanence of cessation and documents post-closure actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of milestone reports to public website
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs with reporting milestones for commitments to permanently cease operations must post their Initial Milestone Report, annual Milestone Status Reports, and Final Milestone Status Report (including schedules and any documentation necessary to demonstrate milestones have been achieved) on the Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website within 30 business days of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This posting requirement ensures public access to closure progress and supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone reporting framework must be flexible to state processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The milestone reporting requirements establish a general framework that is flexible to account for significant differences in retirement/closure processes across jurisdictions; milestones need not be tied to specific times but must be reported relative to the committed cessation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States can explain how their jurisdictional process steps map to required reporting elements and select appropriate milestones accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: General emissions monitoring and reporting requirements (40 CFR part 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs must monitor and report hourly CO2 mass emissions to the atmosphere, total heat input, and total gross electricity output (including useful thermal output converted to gross MWh) in accordance with 40 CFR part 75 monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected EGUs must use a 40 CFR part 75 certified monitoring methodology and report the hourly data on a quarterly basis, with each quarterly report due to the Administrator 30 days after the calendar quarter end.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 CEMS and alternatives for fuel types
rubrics_metrics.description: 40 CFR part 75 monitoring provisions require most coal-fired boilers to use a CO2 continuous emissions monitoring system (CEMS) (CO2 concentration monitor plus stack gas flow monitor). Some oil- and gas-fired boilers may have options to use alternative measurement methodologies (e.g., fuel flow meters combined with fuel quality data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using existing part 75-certified monitors reduces implementation costs and promotes consistency across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 CEMS QA/QC and RATA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each CO2 CEMS must undergo regular quality assurance and quality control activities including periodic relative accuracy test audits (RATAs) comparing the monitoring system to an independent system using EPA reference methods and NIST-traceable calibration gases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA found median differences of about 2% in a May 2022 study; the QA/QC regime addresses concerns about potential bias in CEMS data.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCS-specific monitoring and GHGRP reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs employing CCS must comply with relevant monitoring and reporting under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP, 40 CFR part 98). Facilities that capture and inject CO2 underground must report under GHGRP subpart RR (geologic sequestration) or subpart VV (geologic sequestration with EOR using ISO 27916). Suppliers of CO2 source category (subpart PP) also apply when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the emitting EGU sends captured CO2 offsite, it must transfer it to a facility subject to GHGRP requirements and the injecting facility must report. The emission guideline determines compliance based on tons of CO2 captured by the emitting EGU (not tons sequestered).

rubrics_metrics.name: No change to UIC or downstream regulation in these guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: These emission guidelines do not change requirements to obtain or comply with a UIC permit for facilities subject to the EPA's UIC program, and the guidelines do not regulate downstream recipients of captured CO2; the regulatory standard applies exclusively to the emitting EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leveraging GHGRP reporting avoids duplicative monitoring and ensures the injecting facility maintains responsibility for injection/sequestration reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance flexibilities (trading, averaging, mass-based options) and EPA limits
rubrics_metrics.description: States are permitted to include compliance flexibilities in state plans (e.g., emission trading, averaging, unit-specific mass-based compliance), provided the use of such flexibilities will result in an aggregate level of emission reduction equivalent to each source individually achieving its standard of performance. The EPA may limit flexibilities in an emission guideline if necessary to protect environmental outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters favored mass-based mechanisms for reliability reasons, but final guidance notes fewer affected steam EGUs may limit usefulness of flexibilities. States must design flexibilities consistent with intended environmental outcomes.
